quote: Well, I'm certain of it. There's no question that it's possible. ... So we know that it's feasible, according the laws of physics. Are we able to figure it out well enough? I think that's going to be a matter of time.
claim_summary: Asked by Guy Raz whether we could create an artificial thing that is all around smarter than we are, Brynjolfsson says he is certain it is possible, since the brain is a physical object, and that working it out is a matter of time.
timeline_text: going to be a matter of time
definition_note: interviewer's words: an artificial thing more empathetic, with better judgement, and all around smarter than we are
notes: basis: "I think that's going to be a matter of time"; NPR TED Radio Hour, episode segment "Erik Brynjolfsson: In A Race With Machines, Can We Keep Up?", host Guy Raz; date is the transcript page's publication date (2017-04-21); the interview itself may have been recorded earlier. Read in the NPR transcript. Answer to the question "do you believe it's possible down the line that we could create an artificial thing of metal and ones and zeroes that is more empathetic and exercises better judgement than us and is just all around smarter than we are?" Target superintelligence because the question is about a machine smarter than us all round. "I'm certain of it" is about possibility; the acceptance of arrival rests on "going to be a matter of time". Same interview, earlier: asked whether machines may one day be smarter than us, "No doubt about it. ... They already are much smarter than us at so many things", and "the full implications of the new machine age are going to take at least a century to fully play out" (economic effects, not a capability; not coded). Earlier than the 2017-11-30 statement the panel verification found.

definition_note: true general intelligence = a much broader set of capabilities than humans have; human intelligence is a narrow kind
notes: FT interview by Tej Parikh (FT series of conversations between FT commentators and leading economists), read in the full republication on BizNews (page dated 2024-02-01). Date: month precision 2024-01, because the interview text says generative AI "dominated discussions at Davos this month" and that Robert Solow "passed away last month" (Solow died in December 2023), so it was published in January 2024; the FT original (ft.com/content/b71759fe-397b-4688-bc81-b082edb25f31, linked by Il Foglio) is paywalled and was not read. Target superintelligence because the capabilities "go well beyond what humans have". "let's pursue" raises what to build (governance) without a position on arrival.
